subject: maths
question:
A student was getting the following four offers on the purchase of a book:

I - Two successive discounts of 20% and 20%

II - Two successive discounts of 25% and 15%

III - Two successive discounts of 30% and 10%

lV - Two successive discounts of 5% and 35%

Which scheme offers the most discount to the student?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the sum of two successive discounts is constant, the effective discount is maximized when their numerical difference is maximum.

The sum of the discounts in all four schemes is exactly 40%.

Difference for each scheme: I = 0%, II = 10%, III = 20%, IV = 30%.

Scheme IV has the maximum difference (35% − 5% = 30%), hence it provides the maximum effective discount.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme IV.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Four schemes of successive discounts on a book.

**Formula Used:**

Effective discount for two successive discounts a% and b% = [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%

 Effective Discount Comparison
 Scheme I
 
 36%
 Scheme II
 
 36.25%
 Scheme III
 
 37%
 Scheme IV
 
 38.25% (Max)
 
• 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme I = 20 + 20 − (20 × 20) ÷ 100

⇒ Scheme I = 40 − 4 = 36%

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme II = 25 + 15 − (25 × 15) ÷ 100

⇒ Scheme II = 40 − 3.75 = 36.25%

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme III = 30 + 10 − (30 × 10) ÷ 100

⇒ Scheme III = 40 − 3 = 37%

⇒ Effective discount for Scheme IV = 35 + 5 − (35 × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ Scheme IV = 40 − 1.75 = 38.25%

⇒ Comparing all the calculated effective discounts, 38.25% is the maximum overall discount.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme IV.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are applied on a marked price, the net effective discount is given by the formula: (a + b − a×b÷100)%.

Maximizing Effective Discount

If the sum of multiple successive discounts is constant, the overall discount is highest when the product of the individual discounts is minimized. This occurs when their numerical difference is maximum.

Marked Price & Selling Price

A discount is always calculated over the Marked Price (MP). The Selling Price (SP) after a discount of d% is evaluated as SP = MP × (100 − d)÷100.

Buy X Get Y Free

A widely used alternative discounting model. The effective discount percentage equals (Free items ÷ Total items) × 100.
